grades.quote: Similarly, memorymapped control registers vary in their supported access widths, support for atomic operations, and whether read and write accesses have associated side effects.
grades.reason: Explains that RISC-V distinguishes regions through physical memory attributes. These include cache coherence, atomics and side effects for memory-mapped control registers, and they are checked by a PMA checker. It doesn't name a specific cacheable-versus-device attribute set, so it only partly answers.

grades.quote: The relationship of the memory access type and `MAT` field is: `0` - SUC, `1` - CC, `2` - WUC, and `3` - reserved.
grades.reason: Directly answers the question. LoongArch defines Coherent Cached (CC) and Strongly-ordered or Weakly-ordered Uncached (SUC/WUC) access types, selected by the MAT field. SUC accesses must have no side effects and are used for I/O devices, while CC is for cacheable memory.

grades.quote: provided the corresponding physical addresses are accessible according to the supported access type PMA and are cacheable according to the cacheability PMA
grades.reason: Background on caches and CMO. It mentions that cacheability is governed by a cacheability PMA and an access-type PMA. It doesn't explain how cacheable memory differs from device accesses.

grades.quote: I/O regions can specify which combinations of read, write, or execute accesses to which data widths are supported.
grades.reason: Covers the access-type PMAs and contrasts main memory regions with I/O regions in supported widths and operations. It says nothing about cacheability, so it only partly addresses the distinction.
